decisions.decision: Accept smysl/1.0 in FORMAT_VERSIONS_SUPPORTED while keeping smysl/0.1.
decisions.rationale: The first migration step requires readers to accept both before the writer flips, so old documents keep working and the new version is not refused.
decisions.quote: FORMAT_VERSIONS_SUPPORTED is ["smysl/0.1", "smysl/1.0"] and nothing writes the second yet.

decisions.decision: Add FORMAT_VERSION_DEFAULT, separate from FORMAT_VERSIONS_SUPPORTED[0], and export it from the facade.
decisions.rationale: The two constants stopped meaning the same thing once the supported list grew: one governs what is emitted, the other what is accepted. Embedders need to know the default version to declare.
decisions.quote: FORMAT_VERSION_DEFAULT is new and separate from FORMAT_VERSIONS_SUPPORTED[0], because the two stopped meaning the same thing the moment the list grew: one is what we emit, the other is what we accept.

decisions.decision: Add a format_version field to ParseOutcome and populate it from the parsed @doc header.
decisions.rationale: The parser previously validated and discarded the declared version, so a writer could not preserve it. Storing the version lets a round trip emit what was read.
decisions.quote: ParseOutcome carries the version the document declared;

decisions.decision: Implement a custom Default for ParseOutcome that sets format_version to FORMAT_VERSION_DEFAULT.
decisions.rationale: A derived Default would produce an empty version, which would become an invalid empty @doc header. The CBOR path has no wire version, so the honest default is the current emit version.
decisions.quote: Derived `Default` would give `format_version: ""`, which is not a version and would reach `write_doc` as an empty `@doc` header. The CBOR path builds a `ParseOutcome` this way — the wire has no version to carry — so the honest default is the one this build emits, not the absence of one.

decisions.decision: Add format_version to WriteContext and make write_surface emit it instead of FORMAT_VERSIONS_SUPPORTED[0].
decisions.rationale: The writer should rebuild the header from what the parsed document carried, not from a build-time constant that relabels documents when more than one version is supported.
decisions.quote: WriteContext carries what the header will say; write_surface emits that instead of a build-time constant.

decisions.decision: Pass the parsed format_version from ParseOutcome to WriteContext in `smysl fmt`.
decisions.rationale: `fmt` is the round trip a user runs on purpose and would have been the first place the relabelling bit. Using the declared version preserves the document's self-description.
decisions.quote: `smysl fmt` — the round trip a user runs on purpose — passes one to the other.

decisions.decision: Replace the versioning tripwire count assertion with a round-trip property test for every supported version.
decisions.rationale: The tripwire fired as intended when the list grew. The property it was standing in for is that a document declaring either supported version comes back declaring the one it declared, which a count cannot say.
decisions.quote: What stands in versioning.rs now is the property the count was standing in for: a document declaring either supported version comes back declaring the one it declared.

decisions.decision: Update smysl-core unit tests to loop over FORMAT_VERSIONS_SUPPORTED and reject non-listed near misses (e.g. smysl/2.0).
decisions.rationale: The old test asserted a literal list and used smysl/1.0 as an unknown version. Driving it from the actual list makes it grow with the list instead of failing or silently passing on new versions.
decisions.quote: All four are now driven by the list rather than by a literal, so they grow with it instead of failing on it.

decisions.decision: Strengthen the facade re-export test to check every supported version is accepted and FORMAT_VERSION_DEFAULT is in the supported list.
decisions.rationale: The previous test only checked the first entry, which would have kept passing while a second supported version went unchecked.
decisions.quote: Every declared version must be accepted, not merely the first. The list grew to two in 0.14 and an assertion about `[0]` would have kept passing while the second went unchecked — which is the shape of gap this repository keeps finding.

decisions.decision: Update public API snapshots to include FORMAT_VERSION_DEFAULT and the new smysl-core count.
decisions.rationale: api-check detected the surface growth as intended; adding an export is not a breaking change, so the snapshot must be regenerated.
decisions.quote: api-check caught the surface growing, which is the gate S5 added doing exactly its job: an addition is nobody's break, so semver would not have said a word.

decisions.decision: Update ROAD_TO_1.0.md to mark steps 1 and 2 done, step 3 deferred, and correct the assumption that python/, nodejs/, go/ have version lists.
decisions.rationale: The plan was wrong about the other three implementations because they only read CBOR and never see a @doc header; the migration is Rust-only and smaller than it looked.
decisions.quote: The plan was wrong about the other three implementations.

decisions.decision: Update format spec §8.5 to record the version-trap defect as fixed in 0.14.
decisions.rationale: The trap was invisible until it bit; the spec should now state the fix so the historical warning is replaced with the actual current behavior.
decisions.quote: §8.5 and §8.6 of the format spec updated: the trap is recorded as fixed

decisions.decision: Update format spec §8.6 to say smysl/1.0 is not a break and means the format is settled rather than changed.
decisions.rationale: The version bump signals visibility, not a format change; readers learned the new string quietly, so the compatibility event is the readers' acceptance.
decisions.quote: 8.6 now says what smysl/1.0 will mean, which is that the format is settled rather than changed.

decisions.decision: Defer flipping the writer default to smysl/1.0 until 0.14 is published.
decisions.rationale: §8.2 requires readers to refuse a version absent from their list. Flipping the writer before 0.14 is in the field would make every other implementation reject the output.
decisions.quote: Step 3 — making smysl/1.0 what new documents declare — waits for 0.14 to be published, because §8.2 requires a reader to refuse a version absent from its list: flip the writer before the field has a reader for it and every other implementation rejects the output.

decisions.decision: Do not add version lists to python/, nodejs/, go/ implementations.
decisions.rationale: All three read CBOR only and the wire carries no version string, so no surface parser ever sees a @doc header there. The migration plan's assumption was wrong.
decisions.quote: There is no such list: all three read CBOR only, the wire carries no version string, and go/conformance_test.go says so outright — "surface syntax is not decoded here".

decisions.decision: Do not treat this as a breaking change or require a major version bump.
decisions.rationale: ParseOutcome and WriteContext are #[non_exhaustive], so adding fields does not break embedders, and write_surface's signature never changed. semver remains clean.
decisions.quote: And it is not a breaking change, which is §1.1 paying out: ParseOutcome and WriteContext are both #[non_exhaustive], so each could gain a field without a major bump and write_surface's signature never moved.
